reference.title: Core Strategy
blocks:
- beginner Python syntax
- beginner SQL
- introductory ML courses
- generic "learn AI in 30 days" content
- endless LangChain tutorials
- prompt engineering as a standalone skill
- collecting certifications without practical output
- building many toy chatbots
- learning every LLM provider or framework
- learning every vector database
- studying every AI buzzword
The roadmap optimizes for five outcomes:

1. **Engineering depth** — software engineering, APIs, concurrency, distributed systems, system design.
2. **AI systems depth** — retrieval, LLMs, agents, tools, evaluation, AI reliability.
3. **Production capability** — cloud, containers, CI/CD, observability, performance, security, cost.
4. **Interview readiness** — DSA, system design, ML/AI design, behavioral communication.
5. **Career capital** — flagship projects, GitHub, technical writing, LinkedIn, networking, targeted applications.

reference.title: Sample “Strong Engineer” Thinking Patterns
blocks: > “Retry only transient failures, use bounded exponential backoff with jitter, honor idempotency, use timeouts, avoid retry storms, and combine retries with circuit-breaking or load-shedding when the dependency is unhealthy.”
> “I used a vector database for semantic search.”
> “I compared dense, sparse and hybrid retrieval, measured recall and latency, introduced reranking to improve candidate quality, and evaluated the downstream effect on grounded answer quality.”
> “I separated readiness and liveness behavior, defined resource requests/limits, configured rolling deployment and HPA, and validated scaling behavior with load tests.”

blocks: > **I have 4.5+ years of experience solving AI/ML problems across multiple client environments. My work has covered data science, machine learning, Python engineering and Generative AI/RAG. Avoid framing the transition as simply:

reference.title: Personal Operating Rules
blocks:
1. **Do not learn a technology simply because it is trending.**
2. **Prefer first-party documentation for fast-changing AI technologies.**
3. **Build before consuming another tutorial.**
4. **Benchmark whenever possible.**
5. **Document trade-offs, not only implementation.**
6. **Treat failure modes as part of engineering.**
7. **Do not hide your consulting background; translate it into business impact and ownership.**
8. **Do not expose Deloitte/client confidential information publicly.**
9. **Avoid technology keyword dumping on LinkedIn.**
10. **Do not wait until Month 10 to start networking.**
11. **Use interview feedback as training data.**
12. **Stop studying a topic once the relevant depth/exit criteria are met.**
13. **Prioritize durable concepts over frameworks.**
14. **A project without evaluation/observability is incomplete.**
15. **A production AI system without security, reliability and cost thinking is incomplete.**

reference.title: Final Definition of Success
blocks: This roadmap is successful when the following statement is true:

> **I can take an ambiguous business problem, design a scalable AI architecture, implement the AI and software components, deploy them, evaluate them, observe them, secure them, optimize their cost/latency, and clearly explain my technical and business trade-offs in an interview.**
The objective is not to become the person who knows the most AI tools.
The objective is to become the engineer who can reliably **build and operate AI systems that matter.**
